Name: Squishy / Absorption
Core rule: Proportionally reduces blunt physical impact (Force); may also reduce impulse, knockback and collision.
Identity: Soft tissue yields under impact. Big hits still hurt, but are softened.
Limits and counterplay: Blunt only: cuts (such as a Blood slash) go through normally. Does not resist Acid, Static, Mucus control, Blood effects, Soul or Fire.

Name: Membrane
Core rule: A separate Membrane pool absorbs eligible incoming damage before health. It regenerates after a brief period without Membrane damage.
Identity: Temporary protection that rewards breaking contact. Force is poor at getting through it.
Limits and counterplay: Sustained pressure delays recovery. State and recharge clearly visible (blue; on the player, the existing armour bubble). Does not block already-applied statuses or hazards.
Starting values: 50% of max health; starts to recharge after 2 s without Membrane damage, full in 2 s; Force does 50% to it. Static recharges it (+25% capacity, once per 5 s); there is no supercharge

Name: Shell
Core rule: Finite layers, each subtracting a fixed amount from qualifying physical hits. Each layer has a small amount of its own health. Lost layers are gone for the encounter.
Identity: Rigid protection against repeated small physical hits. One brown ring per layer.
Limits and counterplay: Ordinary hits wear a layer down slowly; Acid's Corrosion strips one much faster; a heavy Force hit knocks one off at once. Layer loss is always visible.
Starting values: 3 off per layer (floor 1); each layer has 15% of max health. Layers: light enemies 1, Diatom 2, Water Bear 4, bosses up to 6

Name: Thorns
Core rule: Returns damage once when a qualifying Contact hit connects. Does not mitigate the hit.
Identity: Makes close-range attacks costly while the attacker keeps its full payoff.
Limits and counterplay: Contact only; ranged attacks and hazards never trigger it. An Evasion miss means no contact and no retaliation. Damage returned is bounded and readable.

Name: Evasion
Core rule: A miss chance against Contact, Projectile and Spread hits (rolled per pellet). A miss shows a visible "miss" puff and avoids the hit and everything attached to it.
Identity: Protection by luck and agility rather than damage reduction or a pool.
Limits and counterplay: Never applies to Burst, Beam or Pool, so area attacks are the reliable answer. Does not clear an existing status or hazard. (Autorun's movement keeps the everyday word "dodge".)
